Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this through the SIG intake. As part of Middleton Bank's procurement for production access we need a compact DR dossier focusing on measurable RTO/RPO evidence and the mechanics for key recovery. Specifically:

- A summary table with committed RTO/RPO numbers by deployment mode (hosted, dedicated, private) and any SLO caveats.
- Recent restore test record (date, duration to first byte, end-to-end restore time).
- Snapshot retention/TTL for primary data stores and embeddings index, and how incremental backups are orchestrated.
- KMS/HSM escrow procedure and whether customer keys are recoverable in an air-gapped scenario.
- Short playbook excerpt showing steps to stand up service from cold (S3 snapshot -> DB restore -> embeddings rebuild -> KV warming).

Can you send a single packet we can attach to our SIG questionnaire? We're on a tight approval cycle and would like to present this at the vendor risk review next Wednesday (2027-06-16). If any items require an NDA or redaction, please flag.

Appreciate it — Monica

Monica —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide a compact packet tailored to Middleton's SIG questionnaire. High-level notes up front:

- Hosted API (multi-tenant): median time-to-first-byte on a restored cold cluster is typically 14–22 minutes depending on region and model family; warm-cache restores (persistent snapshots + KV warmers) bring that down to under 3 minutes for inference-only endpoints.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): we commit an operational RTO of 4 hours for full service resume in the event of AZ-level failure; RPO for customer data artifacts is configurable between 15 minutes and 24 hours depending on retention tier.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): restore cadence depends on customer-run infra; our private control plane provides step-by-step runbooks and can perform assisted restores under contract.

I'll attach: an excerpt of the DR runbook that shows the cold-start playbook, a CSV summary of the RTO/RPO commitments by deployment mode, and our snapshot retention policy. Marissa is copying a short note from ops about last tabletop and live restore runs.

One ask: are you able to share whether Middleton requires KMS customer-key escrow language in the contract or whether a statement of capability suffices for the SIG? If you need a formal escrow agreement, that will route to legal and take a few days.

Deliverables attached: redwood_dr_runbook_excerpt.pdf, rto_rpo_summary_table.csv, snapshot-retention-policy.md. I can also upload a selective video clip from our last restore if that helps (we redact customer ids).

Best,

Hi Monica / Kimberly,

Adding a few technical specifics for the packet and clarifying test artifacts we can include: 

- Last live restore test (internal): 2027-05-27T02:14:00Z — complete restore (S3 snapshot -> DB restore -> embeddings rebuild -> KV warm) measured at 2h 18m for the full cluster used in that exercise. We can provide the run log excerpt (redacted).
- Incremental backups: levelled incremental snapshots every 15 minutes for delta layers, full snapshots nightly (00:00 UTC). RPO is therefore configurable; for our standard enterprise tier we operate 15m RPO with 30-day warm retention and 365-day cold retention.
- Embeddings index rebuild: parallelized map-reduce rebuild, sample timing for a 3TB index rebuild on our dedicated pool historically ~1.4–2.0 hours depending on model tokenizer overhead. We include a small timing matrix in the CSV.
- KMS/HSM escrow: we use customer-managed keys where required; the escrow flow is: key wrap -> HSM-managed export token -> 2-of-3 key-holders escrow (legal/compliance/ops). We cannot provide raw key material but we can provide signed attestations of the escrow procedure and an HSM audit extract for the escrow event. Attached: kms-hsm-escrow-steps.pdf.

Attachments included in packet: redwood_dr_runbook_excerpt.pdf (playbook excerpt), rto_rpo_summary_table.csv (timings and caveats), snapshot-retention-policy.md, kms-hsm-escrow-steps.pdf.

If Middleton needs a witnessed session (live or recorded) for the vendor risk panel, we can schedule a 30-minute walk-through with our ops lead (Sojin) and provide a sanitized log package and a short restore clip.
